messages.text: I’ll read the frozen brief, inspect the lane, then add the golden and run its required validation.
The existing Java wildcard golden already uses a test-only Files model and renders native call bindings. I’ll extend that fixture with the requested cases.
The focused golden is compiling. Once it runs, I’ll inspect the per-site results before accepting any expected-file changes.

The new cases render as requested on the branch: the cast and typed local select, while the different-owner, wildcard, poly, and incomplete-bound cases remain unproven. I’ll run the same fixture on the base next to identify which expected-file changes belong to this branch.
The base comparison is still compiling through mbx. I also found a formatting difference from the new test attribute and applied `cargo fmt`; I’ll check the final diff after the base run.

The golden is committed as `09b4a9c746`. The base comparison confirms that the cast and typed `Iterable<CharSequence>` cases change from unproven to selected. The byte-array control stays selected; the `Iterable<Object>` control changes from unproven to rejected. I’ll continue with the remaining gates and the two revert proofs.

The workspace check passed. I’m running the first isolation proof with the Java containment slice temporarily restored to its pre-change version; the command will restore the branch files after it captures the result.

Both isolation proofs passed: reverting either transport or containment makes the cast and typed local unproven again. The JVM selection is compiling now; I’ll classify any failures against the base before changing expected output.
The JVM selection finished with one failure in a tools SQL-count test; 2,082 other tests passed. I’ll run the same selection on the base to determine whether the failure predates this branch.

The tools SQL-count test fails identically on the base: its assertion expects one read and sees two. That makes it a baseline failure for this branch. I’ll finish the base selection, then continue the remaining validation, including the scheduled JVM tests the parent added.

The Go selection ran 1,029 tests and has three failures, including a Rust control-analysis golden selected by the broad `go` name filter. I’m running the same selection on the base before classifying them. No Go expected files have been changed.

The Go selection has the same three failures on the base, including the same Rust golden hash difference. The branch remains clean and no Go golden changed. I’m moving to the full policy integration suite.

Policy integration has the same ten failures on the base and branch. The logs show cache I/O errors at a path outside this lane for several of them; I have not blessed those outputs. I’m running CI’s two Clippy commands next, followed by the identity and scheduled JVM checks.

Both identity tests and both Clippy commands passed. I’ve started the scheduled JVM selection with `--cfg scheduled_tests` and JDK 21. That flag rebuilds the test binaries, so this phase will take longer.

The scheduled default run completed: 502 passed, ten failed, and the native JVM usage differential timed out at nextest’s 600-second limit. Several failures are indexed JDK expectations; I’ll compare the exact selection on the base before classifying any as branch defects.

The base scheduled run is reproducing the early indexed JDK and annotation golden failures. I’m letting the full selection finish so I can compare its complete failure set, including the long usage test, before running the trial route.
The scheduled default base run matched the branch: 502 passed, the same ten failed, and the same usage differential timed out at 600 seconds. I’ve started the scheduled trial route with the real JDK.

The scheduled trial run finished with 498 passed, fourteen failed, and the usage differential timed out. I’m running the identical trial selection on the base now. Once it finishes, I’ll compare the failure names and outputs and hand back the evidence.
